name: The Danube Bend
region: Pest and Komárom-Esztergom, north of Budapest
tagline: Where the Danube swings south through forested hills, a string of artists' towns, a hilltop citadel and Hungary's grandest basilica.
highlight: The view from Visegrád's citadel over the Danube's great S-shaped bend.
shortDescription: A day-trip loop from Budapest to the baroque artists' town of Szentendre, the royal citadel at Visegrád and the basilica at Esztergom, along a picturesque stretch of the Danube.
metaDescription: A Danube Bend travel guide: Szentendre, Visegrád Citadel, Esztergom Basilica, how to do it as a day trip from Budapest by train, boat and bus, food, and a one-day plan.
goodFor: Day trips, art, history, river views

image.alt: The Danube bending between forested hills at Visegrád

intro: North of Budapest, the Danube turns sharply from its eastward course toward the south, forming an S-shaped bend between the Börzsöny and Pilis hills. The scenery is green and hilly, and the river valley has been settled for centuries. Three towns make up the classic day trip: Szentendre, Visegrád and Esztergom.

Szentendre is a small baroque town of cobbled lanes, colourful houses and art galleries, settled by Serbian refugees in the 17th century, whose Orthodox churches still stand. Visegrád was a royal seat in the 14th and 15th centuries, and its hilltop citadel gives the finest views of the bend. Esztergom, the birthplace of King Stephen and the seat of Hungary's Catholic church, has the country's largest church, a domed basilica above the river opposite Slovakia.

All three can be reached from Budapest by train, bus or boat, and together they make a rewarding day trip, though a long one. Many visitors pick two, for example Szentendre and Visegrád, or spend a night.

whyVisit.intro: The Danube Bend is the easiest scenic escape from the capital.

attractionsIntro: The three towns are 20 to 50 km apart along the river.

attractions.name: Szentendre

image.alt: Colourful houses on the main square of Szentendre

attractions.text: A pretty town of cobbled lanes, galleries, museums and Serbian Orthodox churches, only 40 minutes from Budapest by suburban train.

attractions.name: Visegrád Citadel

image.alt: The Danube and the hills at Visegrád

attractions.text: A hilltop fortress with views of the Danube Bend, near the ruins of a royal palace of the 14th century.
attractions.tip: Take a taxi or bus up.

attractions.name: Esztergom Basilica

image.alt: The domed Esztergom Basilica beside the Danube

attractions.text: Hungary's largest church, with a dome visible for miles, built in the 19th century on the site of the country's first cathedral.

attractions.name: Royal Palace of Visegrád
attractions.text: Ruins of a Renaissance palace, with a Hercules fountain.

attractions.name: Esztergom Castle
attractions.text: The birthplace of King Stephen, with a museum.

attractions.name: Pilis hills
attractions.text: Forests and hiking above the river.

thingsToDoIntro: The bend is about towns and views.

thingsToDo.title: Cross into Slovakia
thingsToDo.text: Walk across the Mária Valéria Bridge.

foodIntro: The Bend's food is simple, with riverside fish.

accommodation.intro: Most visitors return to Budapest, but Szentendre suits a night.

gettingThere.intro: All three are reachable from Budapest.

options.text: Boats to Visegrád in summer, buses in all seasons.

bestTime.headline: April–October
bestTime.summary: The Bend is best in spring and autumn.
